rows.name: Bael
rows.office: Makes thee go invisible. His character must be worn as a lamen before the one who calls him forth, or he will not do homage.
rows.rank_text: a King ruling in the East ("The First Principal Spirit")
rows.appearance: In divers shapes: sometimes like a cat, sometimes like a toad, sometimes like a man, and sometimes all these forms at once. Speaks hoarsely.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Invisibility; wisdom. Appears as cat, toad, man, or all three.

rows.name: Agares (Agreas)
rows.office: Makes those who stand still run and brings back runaways; teaches all languages or tongues at once; has power to destroy dignities both spiritual and temporal; causes earthquakes.
rows.rank_text: a Duke, under the Power of the East (he was of the Order of Virtues)
rows.appearance: In the form of an old fair man, riding upon a crocodile, carrying a goshawk upon his fist, and yet mild in appearance.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Teaches languages; returns runaways; causes earthquakes; destroys dignities.

rows.name: Vassago
rows.office: Of a good nature. Declares things past and to come, and discovers all things hid or lost.
rows.rank_text: a Mighty Prince, being of the same nature as Agares
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Past and future; finds things lost or hidden. Reputedly good-natured.

rows.name: Samigina (Gamigin)
rows.office: Teaches all liberal sciences; gives account of dead souls that died in sin.
rows.appearance: In the form of a little horse or ass; then, at the request of the Master, he changes himself into human shape. Speaks with a hoarse voice.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Liberal sciences; gives account of souls that died in sin / the drowned.

rows.name: Marbas
rows.office: Answers truly of things hidden or secret; causes and cures diseases; gives great wisdom and knowledge in mechanical arts; can change men into other shapes.
rows.appearance: At first in the form of a great lion; afterwards, at the request of the Master, he puts on human shape.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Hidden and secret things; causes and cures disease; mechanical arts; shape-change.

rows.name: Valefor
rows.office: A good familiar, but tempts those he is a familiar of to steal. His seal is worn whether or not you take him as a familiar.
rows.appearance: In the shape of a lion with an ass's head, bellowing.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Familiar to thieves; tempts to steal. Keep a close hand.

rows.name: Amon
rows.office: Tells all things past and to come; procures feuds and reconciles controversies between friends.
rows.rank_text: a Marquis great in power, and most stern
rows.appearance: Like a wolf with a serpent's tail, vomiting flames of fire out of his mouth; at the command of the Magician he puts on the shape of a man with dog's teeth beset in a head like a raven, or else simply a man with a raven's head.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Past and future; procures love; reconciles friends and foes.

rows.name: Barbatos
rows.office: Gives understanding of the singing of birds and the voices of other creatures, such as the barking of dogs; breaks open hidden treasures laid by the enchantments of magicians; knows all things past and to come; conciliates friends and those in power.
rows.rank_text: a Great Duke (of the Order of Virtues, of which some part he retaineth still)
rows.appearance: When the Sun is in Sagittary, with four noble Kings and their companies of great troops. No bodily form is described.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Speech of animals; treasure hidden by magicians; reconciliation; past and future.

rows.name: Paimon
rows.office: Teaches all arts and sciences and other secret things; can tell what the Earth is and what holds it up in the Waters, what Mind is and where it is, or any other thing you desire to know; gives dignity and confirms it; binds or makes any man subject to the Magician; gives good familiars, such as can teach all arts. Is to be observed towards the West. If called alone, he must be made some offering.
rows.rank_text: a Great King, and very obedient unto LUCIFER (of the Order of Dominations, or Dominions)
rows.legions: 200 (part of the Order of Angels, the other part of Potentates). If called alone, two Kings, LABAL and ABALIM, attend him with other spirits of the Order of Potentates in his host, and 25 Legions.
rows.appearance: In the form of a man sitting upon a dromedary, with a most glorious crown upon his head. Before him goes a host of spirits like men with trumpets, well-sounding cymbals and all other sorts of musical instruments. He has a great voice and roars at his first coming, and his speech is such that the Magician cannot well understand it unless he can compel him.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: All arts and sciences; binds men to the magician; gives dignities and familiars. Attends Lucifer.

rows.name: Buer
rows.office: Teaches moral and natural philosophy, logic, and the virtues of all herbs and plants; heals all distempers in man; gives good familiars.
rows.appearance: In Sagittary, and that is his shape when the Sun is there.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Philosophy, logic, ethics; virtues of herbs; heals distempers; familiars.

rows.name: Gusion
rows.office: Tells all things past, present and to come, and shows the meaning and resolution of all questions; conciliates and reconciles friendships; gives honour and dignity.
rows.appearance: Like a Xenopilus.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Past, present, future; answers all questions; honour and dignity; reconciles.

rows.name: Sitri
rows.office: Enflames men with women's love and women with men's love, and causes them to show themselves naked if desired.
rows.appearance: At first with a leopard's head and the wings of a gryphon; after the command of the Master of the Exorcism he puts on a very beautiful human shape.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Enflames love between the sexes; makes people show themselves naked.

rows.name: Beleth (Bileth)
rows.office: Causes all the love that may be, both of men and of women, until the Master Exorcist has had his desire fulfilled. Of the Order of Powers. The exorcist lays his courage with a hazel wand struck out towards the South and East, makes a triangle outside the circle and commands him into it by the Bonds and Charges; he must be received courteously, with homage, as a great King, and a silver ring is worn on the middle finger of the left hand, held against the face, as before Amaymon.
rows.rank_text: a mighty King and terrible (also 'a Great King'; of the Order of Powers)
rows.appearance: Riding on a pale horse, with trumpets and other kinds of musical instruments playing before him; very furious at his first appearance.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Love between men and women. Fierce on arrival; requires a hazel wand and courtesy.

rows.name: Leraje (Leraikha)
rows.office: Causes all great battles and contests; makes wounds made with arrows by archers putrefy. This belongs unto Sagittary.
rows.appearance: In the likeness of an archer clad in green, carrying a bow and quiver.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Great battles and contests; makes arrow wounds putrefy.

rows.name: Eligos
rows.office: Discovers hidden things and knows things to come, and of wars and how the soldiers will or shall meet; causes the love of lords and great persons.
rows.appearance: In the form of a goodly knight, carrying a lance, an ensign and a serpent.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Hidden things; knowledge of wars and how they fall out; love of lords and great persons.

rows.name: Zepar
rows.office: Causes women to love men and brings them together in love; also makes them barren.
rows.appearance: In red apparel and armour, like a soldier.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Makes women love men; can also make them barren.

rows.name: Botis
rows.office: Tells all things past and to come; reconciles friends and foes.
rows.rank_text: a Great President, and an Earl
rows.appearance: At first in the form of an ugly viper; then, at the magician's command, he puts on a human shape with great teeth and two horns, carrying a bright and sharp sword in his hand.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Past and future; reconciles friends and foes.

rows.name: Bathin
rows.office: Knows the virtues of herbs and precious stones; can transport men suddenly from one country to another.
rows.appearance: Like a strong man with the tail of a serpent, sitting upon a pale-coloured [horse?] (Mathers brackets 'horse' as uncertain in the codices; Crowley's editorial note: the Quartos have 'ass').
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Virtues of herbs and precious stones; carries people from country to country.

rows.name: Sallos (Saleos)
rows.office: Causes the love of women for men and of men for women.
rows.appearance: A gallant soldier riding a crocodile, wearing a ducal crown; comes peaceably.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Love between the sexes. Peaceable.

rows.name: Purson
rows.office: Knows hidden things and finds treasure; tells past, present and future; answers truly about earthly things, secret and divine, and the creation of the world; gives good familiars.
rows.legions: 22 (partly of the Order of Virtues and partly of the Order of Thrones)
rows.appearance: A comely man with a lion's face, carrying a cruel viper and riding a bear, with many trumpets sounding before him. Can take a human or aerial body.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Hidden things; finds treasure; past, present, future; good familiars.

rows.name: Marax (Morax)
rows.office: Makes men very knowing in astronomy and all the liberal sciences; gives good, wise familiars who know the virtues of herbs and precious stones.
rows.appearance: A great bull with a man's face.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Astronomy and liberal sciences; virtues of herbs and precious stones; wise familiars.

rows.name: Ipos
rows.office: Knows all things past, present and to come; makes men witty and bold.
rows.rank_text: an Earl, and a Mighty Prince
rows.appearance: An angel with a lion's head, a goose's foot and a hare's tail.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Past and future; makes men witty and bold.

rows.name: Aim
rows.office: Sets cities, castles and great places on fire; makes one witty in all ways; gives true answers about private matters.
rows.appearance: A very handsome man with three heads: a serpent, a man with two stars on his forehead, and a calf. Rides a viper and carries a firebrand.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Sets cities, castles and great places on fire; makes men witty; secret matters.

rows.name: Naberius
rows.office: Makes men cunning in all arts and sciences, especially rhetoric; restores lost dignities and honours.
rows.appearance: A black crane fluttering about the circle; speaks with a hoarse voice.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Arts and sciences, especially rhetoric; restores lost dignities and honours.

rows.name: Glasya-Labolas
rows.office: Teaches all arts and sciences in an instant, and all things past and to come; author of bloodshed and manslaughter; causes the love of friends and foes; makes a man invisible.
rows.appearance: A dog with wings like a gryphon.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Arts and sciences instantly; author of bloodshed and manslaughter; invisibility; love of friends and foes.

rows.name: Bune (Bimé)
rows.office: Changes the place of the dead and makes the spirits under him gather on your sepulchres; gives riches, wisdom and eloquence; gives true answers to demands. Has two seals; the second (fig. 31) is the better.
rows.rank_text: a Strong, Great and Mighty Duke
rows.appearance: A dragon with three heads: one like a dog, one like a gryphon, one like a man. Speaks with a high and comely voice.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Changes the place of the dead; gives riches, wisdom and eloquence; his demons gather on sepulchres.

rows.name: Ronové
rows.office: Teaches rhetoric very well; gives good servants, knowledge of tongues, and favour with friends or foes.
rows.appearance: In the form of a monster.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Rhetoric, languages; good servants; favour of friends and foes.

rows.name: Berith (Beale)
rows.office: Gives true answers of past, present and to come; turns all metals into gold; gives dignities and confirms them. A great liar, not to be trusted (a footnote remarks this hardly agrees with his true answers). Use a ring in calling him, as with Beleth.
rows.rank_text: a Mighty, Great, and Terrible Duke
rows.appearance: A soldier in red clothing, riding a red horse, with a crown of gold on his head. Speaks with a very clear and subtle voice.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_variant: Heb. berīt 'covenant'; Baal-Berith — Ar. Bible بَعْل بَرِيث (Judg 8:33)
rows.workbook_office: Turns all metals to gold; gives dignities; past, present, future. A great liar; use the ring.

rows.name: Astaroth
rows.office: Gives true answers of past, present and to come; discovers all secrets; declares, if desired, how the spirits fell and the reason of his own fall; makes men wonderfully knowing in all liberal sciences. Hold the magical ring near your face against his breath, and wear his seal as a lamen or he will not appear or obey.
rows.appearance: A hurtful angel riding an infernal beast like a dragon, carrying a viper in his right hand. His noisome breath does damage if he comes too near.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_variant: Semitic ʿAshtoreth / Ishtar — Ar. Bible عَشْتَارُوث; Ar. عِشْتَار
rows.workbook_office: Past, present, future; all secrets; liberal sciences; how the spirits fell. Hold the ring against his breath.

rows.name: Forneus
rows.office: Teaches rhetoric and makes men wonderfully knowing in it; gives a good name and the knowledge and understanding of tongues; makes one beloved of foes as well as friends.
rows.legions: 29 (partly of the Order of Thrones, partly of that of Angels)
rows.appearance: A great sea-monster.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Rhetoric; languages; good name; makes enemies love you.

rows.name: Foras
rows.office: Gives understanding of the virtues of all herbs and precious stones; teaches logic and ethics in all their parts; if desired, makes men invisible (one or two codices: 'invincible'), long-lived and eloquent; discovers treasures and recovers things lost.
rows.appearance: A strong man in human shape.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Virtues of herbs and stones; logic and ethics; invisibility; long life; eloquence; finds treasure.

rows.name: Asmoday (Asmodai)
rows.office: Gives the Ring of Virtues; teaches arithmetic, astronomy, geometry and all handicrafts; gives true and full answers; makes one invincible; shows where treasure lies and guards it. First and choicest under Amaymon, going before all others. Call him abroad, standing, with cap or head-dress off (if it is on, Amaymon will deceive you and bewray your actions); ask 'Art thou Asmoday?' and he will not deny it but will bow to the ground. Wear his seal as a lamen on your breast.
rows.rank_text: a Great King, Strong, and Powerful
rows.legions: 72 (Inferior Spirits, among the Legions of Amaymon)
rows.appearance: Three heads (bull, man, ram), a serpent's tail, flames of fire from his mouth, and feet webbed like a goose's. Sits on an infernal dragon and bears a lance with a banner.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_variant: Heb./Aram. Ashmedai أَشْمَدَاي; Ar. Tobit أَسْمُودَاوُس
rows.workbook_office: The ring of virtues; arithmetic, astronomy, geometry, handicrafts; treasure; invincibility. Attends Amaymon.

rows.name: Gäap
rows.office: Makes men insensible or ignorant, or knowing in philosophy and all liberal sciences; causes love or hatred; teaches how to consecrate the things of the dominion of Amaymon, his King; delivers familiars out of the custody of other magicians; answers truly and perfectly of past, present and to come; carries men speedily from one kingdom to another at the exorcist's will. He was of the Order of Potentates.
rows.rank_text: a Great President and a Mighty Prince
rows.appearance: Human shape. He appears when the Sun is in some of the southern signs, going before four great and mighty kings as if he were a guide to conduct them on their way.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Philosophy and liberal sciences; love and hatred; carries men between kingdoms; familiars of other magicians. Governs the South (Goetia).

rows.name: Furfur
rows.office: Never speaks truth unless compelled or brought up within a triangle; urges love between man and woman; raises lightnings and thunders, blasts and great tempestuous storms; if commanded, gives true answers of things secret and divine.
rows.appearance: A hart with a fiery tail. Within the triangle he takes the form of an angel, and when bidden speaks with a hoarse voice.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Love between man and wife; thunder, lightning, storms; secret and divine things. Lies unless in the triangle.

rows.name: Marchosias
rows.office: A strong fighter. He was of the Order of Dominations; told his chief, Solomon, that after 1,200 years he hoped to return to the Seventh Throne.
rows.appearance: At first a wolf with gryphon's wings and a serpent's tail, vomiting fire; after a time, at the exorcist's command, he takes the shape of a man. A footnote says one badly written seventeenth-century codex might read 'Ox' for 'Wolf'; Crowley (ED.) adds that for him he always appeared as an ox, and very dazed.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Strong fighter; true answers; faithful to the exorcist. Hopes to return to the Seventh Throne.

rows.name: Stolas (Stolos)
rows.office: Teaches the art of astronomy and the virtues of herbs and precious stones.
rows.appearance: At first a mighty raven before the exorcist; afterwards the image of a man.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Astronomy; virtues of herbs and precious stones.

rows.name: Phenex (Pheynix)
rows.office: Once in human shape, speaks marvellously of all wonderful sciences if required; a good and excellent poet, willing to perform requests. Hopes to return to the Seventh Throne after 1,200 years more.
rows.appearance: Like the bird Phœnix, having the voice of a child. He sings many sweet notes before the exorcist, which the exorcist must not heed; by-and-by the exorcist must bid him put on human shape.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: All wonderful sciences; excellent poet. Hopes to return to the Seventh Throne.

rows.name: Halphas (Malthus)
rows.office: Builds up towers and furnishes them with ammunition and weapons; sends men-of-war (warriors, men-at-arms) to places appointed.
rows.appearance: In the form of a stock-dove, speaking with a hoarse voice.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Builds towers and furnishes them with ammunition and weapons; sends men to war.

rows.name: Malphas
rows.office: Builds houses and high towers; reveals enemies' desires, thoughts and deeds; gives good familiars. Receives sacrifice kindly and willingly but deceives the one who offers it.
rows.appearance: At first like a crow; afterwards puts on human shape at the exorcist's request and speaks with a hoarse voice.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Builds houses and high towers; brings artificers; destroys enemies' desires and works; familiars.

rows.name: Räum
rows.office: Steals treasures out of kings' houses and carries them where commanded; destroys cities and dignities of men; tells all things past, present and to come; causes love between friends and foes. Formerly of the Order of Thrones.
rows.appearance: At first in the form of a crow; at the exorcist's command he puts on human shape.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Steals treasure out of kings' houses; destroys cities and dignities; past, present, future; love between friends and foes.

rows.name: Focalor (Forcalor)
rows.office: Slays men and drowns them in the waters; overthrows ships of war, having power over both winds and seas; but will not hurt any man or thing if the exorcist commands to the contrary. Hopes to return to the Seventh Throne after 1,000 years.
rows.legions: 30 (Mathers' footnote: several codices give three instead of 30, but 30 is probably more correct)
rows.appearance: In the form of a man with gryphon's wings.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Kills men, drowns them, overthrows ships; power over winds and seas.

rows.name: Vepar (Vephar)
rows.office: Governs the waters and guides ships laden with arms, armour and ammunition; at request makes the seas stormy and appear full of ships; makes men die in three days of putrefying wounds or sores in which worms breed.
rows.appearance: Like a mermaid.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Governs the waters; guides ships laden with arms; storms at sea; makes wounds putrefy.

rows.name: Sabnock (Savnok)
rows.office: Builds high towers, castles and cities and furnishes them with armour; afflicts men for many days with wounds and sores, rotten and full of worms; gives good familiars at the exorcist's request.
rows.rank_text: a Marquis, Mighty, Great and Strong
rows.appearance: In the form of an armed soldier with a lion's head, riding on a pale-coloured horse.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Builds high towers, castles and cities; afflicts with wounds and worms; good familiars.

rows.name: Shax (Shaz)
rows.office: At the exorcist's command takes away the sight, hearing or understanding of any man or woman; steals money out of the houses of kings and carries it again in 1,200 years; fetches horses or any other thing when commanded; discovers all hidden things not kept by wicked spirits; sometimes gives good familiars. Must first be commanded into a triangle, or he deceives and tells many lies.
rows.appearance: In the form of a stock-dove, speaking with a hoarse but subtle voice.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Takes away sight, hearing and understanding; steals money; fetches horses; hidden things. Lies unless in the triangle.

rows.name: Viné (Vinea)
rows.office: Discovers things hidden, witches, wizards, and things present, past and to come; at the exorcist's command builds towers, overthrows great stone walls and makes the waters rough with storms.
rows.rank_text: a Great King, and an Earl
rows.appearance: In the form of a lion (Mathers' note: some codices say with a lion's head), riding a black horse and bearing a viper in his hand.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Hidden things; witches and wizards; past, present, future; builds towers; overthrows walls; troubles waters.

rows.name: Bifrons (Bifröus)
rows.office: Astrology, geometry and other arts and sciences; virtues of precious stones and woods; changes dead bodies and puts them in another place; lights seeming candles on graves.
rows.legions: 6 (note: unsigned footnote, by Mathers as translator: 'Should probably be 60 instead of 6.')
rows.appearance: A monster; after a while, at the exorcist's command, he takes the shape of a man.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Astrology, geometry, arts and sciences; herbs, stones, woods; moves bodies and lights candles on graves.

rows.name: Uvall (Vual)
rows.office: Love of women; past, present, future; friendship between friends and foes.
rows.rank_text: a Duke, Great, Mighty, and Strong
rows.appearance: At first a mighty dromedary; after a while, at the exorcist's command, he takes human shape and speaks the Egyptian tongue, but not perfectly. (Crowley's note: 'He can nowadays converse in sound though colloquial Coptic.')
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Love of women; past, present, future; friendship between friends and foes.

rows.name: Haagenti
rows.office: Makes men wise and instructs them in divers things; transmutes all metals into gold; changes wine into water and water into wine.
rows.appearance: At first a mighty bull with gryphon's wings; afterwards, at the exorcist's command, human shape.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Wisdom; transmutes metals into gold, wine into water and water into wine.

rows.name: Crocell (Crokel)
rows.office: Teaches the art of geometry and the liberal sciences; at the exorcist's command makes great noises like the rushings of many waters, although there be none; warms waters and discovers baths.
rows.appearance: An angel; speaks somewhat mystically of hidden things.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Geometry and liberal sciences; hidden things; warms waters and discovers baths.

rows.name: Furcas
rows.office: Philosophy, astrology, rhetoric, logic, cheiromancy and pyromancy, in all their parts and perfectly.
rows.appearance: A cruel old man with a long beard and a hoary head, riding a pale-coloured horse, with a sharp weapon in his hand.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Philosophy, astronomy, rhetoric, logic, chiromancy, pyromancy.

rows.name: Balam (Balaam)
rows.office: Gives true answers of things past, present and to come; makes men go invisible, and also to be witty.
rows.rank_text: a Terrible, Great, and Powerful King
rows.appearance: Three heads (a bull's, a man's, a ram's), a serpent's tail and flaming eyes; rides a furious bear and carries a goshawk on his fist; speaks with a hoarse voice.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Past, present, future; invisibility; wit.

rows.name: Alloces (Alocas)
rows.office: Teaches the art of astronomy and all the liberal sciences; brings good familiars.
rows.rank_text: a Duke, Great, Mighty, and Strong
rows.appearance: A soldier (Mathers's note: 'Or Warrior') riding a great horse; his face like a lion's, very red, with flaming eyes; his speech hoarse and very big.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Astronomy and liberal sciences; good familiars.

rows.name: Camio (Caïm)
rows.office: Understanding of all birds, the lowing of bullocks, the barking of dogs and other creatures, and the voice of the waters; true answers of things to come.
rows.appearance: At first a thrush; afterwards a man carrying a sharp sword in his hand; seems to answer in burning ashes or coals of fire. A good disputer.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Speech of birds, cattle, dogs and waters; things to come.

rows.name: Murmur (Murmus)
rows.office: Philosophy; constrains souls of the dead to appear and answer.
rows.rank_text: a Great Duke, and an Earl
rows.appearance: A warrior riding a gryphon, with a ducal crown on his head; his ministers go before him sounding great trumpets.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Philosophy; constrains souls of the dead to appear and answer.

rows.name: Orobas
rows.office: Discovers all things past, present and to come; gives dignities and prelacies, and the favour of friends and foes; gives true answers of divinity and of the creation of the world. Very faithful to the exorcist, whom he will not suffer to be tempted by any spirit.
rows.appearance: At first like a horse; after the exorcist's command he puts on the image of a man.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Past, present, future; dignities and prelacies; favour of friends and foes. Faithful; will not deceive.

rows.name: Gremory (Gamori)
rows.office: Tells of all things past, present and to come, and of treasures hid, and what they lie in; procures the love of women both young and old.
rows.appearance: A beautiful woman with a duchess's crown tied about her waist, riding a great camel.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Past, present, future; hidden treasure; love of women, young and old.

rows.name: Osé (Voso)
rows.office: Makes one cunning in the liberal sciences; gives true answers of divine and secret things; changes a man into any shape the exorcist pleases, so that he believes he truly is the creature or thing he is changed into.
rows.legions: 3 (1904 footnote: "Should probably be 30. For these 72 Great Spirits of the Book Goetia are all Princes and Leaders of numbers.")
rows.appearance: At first like a leopard; after a little time he puts on the shape of a man.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Liberal sciences; true answers on divine and secret things; changes a man into any shape; delusion.

rows.name: Amy (Avnas)
rows.office: Makes one wonderfully knowing in astrology and all the liberal sciences; gives good familiars; can bewray treasure that is kept by spirits.
rows.appearance: At first a flaming fire; after a while he puts on the shape of a man.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Astrology and liberal sciences; good familiars; treasure kept by spirits.

rows.name: Oriax (Orias)
rows.office: Teaches the virtues of the stars, the mansions of the planets and how to understand their virtues; transforms men; gives dignities, prelacies and their confirmation; favour with friends and foes.
rows.appearance: A lion (note: or 'with the face of a lion') riding a mighty, strong horse with a serpent's tail (editor's note asks whether the tail is the horse's or the Marquis's), holding two great hissing serpents in his right hand.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Virtues of the stars and planets; transforms men; dignities and confirmations; favour.

rows.name: Vapula (Naphula)
rows.office: Makes men knowing in all handicrafts and professions, also in philosophy and other sciences.
rows.rank_text: a Duke Great, Mighty, and Strong
rows.appearance: A lion with gryphon's wings.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Handicrafts and professions; philosophy and sciences.

rows.name: Zagan
rows.office: Makes men witty; turns wine into water, blood into wine, water into wine; turns all metals into coin of the dominion that metal is of; can make even fools wise.
rows.appearance: At first a bull with gryphon's wings; after a while he puts on human shape.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Makes men witty; turns wine into water, blood into wine, water into wine, metals into coin; makes fools wise.

rows.name: Volac (Valak)
rows.office: Gives true answers of hidden treasures; tells where serpents may be seen, and brings them to the exorciser without any force or strength being employed by him.
rows.appearance: A child with angel's wings, riding a two-headed dragon.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Hidden treasures; where serpents may be seen.

rows.name: Andras
rows.office: Sows discords. If the exorcist is not careful, he will slay both him and his fellows.
rows.appearance: An angel with a head like a black night raven, riding a strong black wolf, with a sharp, bright sword flourished aloft in his hand.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Sows discord. Will kill the magician and assistants if not careful.

rows.name: Haures (Hauras)
rows.office: Gives true answers of all things present, past and to come, but if he is not commanded into a triangle he lies in all these things and deceives and beguiles the exorcist. Lastly, talks of the creation of the world, of divinity, and of how he and other spirits fell. Destroys and burns up the exorcist's enemies if he so desires, and will not let him be tempted by any other spirit or otherwise.
rows.appearance: At first like a leopard, mighty, terrible and strong; after a while, at the exorcist's command, he puts on human shape with eyes flaming and fiery, and a most terrible countenance.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Past, present, future; destroys and burns enemies; true answers on divinity and the fall. Lies unless in the triangle.

rows.name: Andrealphus
rows.office: Teaches geometry perfectly and makes men very subtle in it and in everything to do with mensuration or astronomy; can transform a man into the likeness of a bird.
rows.appearance: At first in the form of a peacock, with great noises; after a time he puts on human shape.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Geometry and mensuration; astronomy; transforms men into birds.

rows.name: Cimejes (Cimeies)
rows.office: Rules all spirits in the parts of Africa; teaches grammar, logic and rhetoric perfectly; discovers things lost or hidden, and treasures.
rows.rank_text: a Marquis, Mighty, Great, Strong and Powerful
rows.appearance: Like a valiant warrior riding upon a goodly black horse.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Grammar, logic, rhetoric; lost and hidden things; treasure; rules the spirits of Africa.

rows.name: Amdusias (Amdukias)
rows.office: Causes trumpets and all manner of musical instruments to be heard, 'but not soon or immediately'; makes trees bend and incline at the exorcist's will; gives excellent familiars.
rows.appearance: At first like a unicorn; at the exorcist's request he stands before him in human shape.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Music heard but unseen; makes trees bend; excellent familiars.

rows.name: Belial
rows.office: Created next after Lucifer; declares that he fell first from among the worthier sort that were before Michael and other heavenly angels. Distributes presentations and senatorships; causes favour of friends and of foes; gives excellent familiars. He must have offerings, sacrifices and gifts presented by the exorcist or he will not give true answers, and even then he does not stay one hour in the truth unless constrained by divine power.
rows.rank_text: a Mighty and a Powerful King
rows.legions: 80 (notes: Mathers suggests 30; Crowley says 50, 'at least it was in 1898')
rows.appearance: In the form of two beautiful angels sitting in a chariot of fire; speaks with a comely voice.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_variant: Heb. Beliyaʿal — Ar. Bible بَلِيعَال (2 Cor 6:15)
rows.workbook_office: Dignities; favour of friends and foes; excellent familiars. Requires offerings; created next after Lucifer.

rows.name: Decarabia
rows.office: Discovers the virtues of birds and precious stones; makes the likeness of all kinds of birds fly before the exorcist, singing and drinking as natural birds do.
rows.rank_text: a Great Marquis ("being himself a Great Marquis")
rows.appearance: At first in the form of a star in a pentacle (⛤); after, at the exorcist's command, he puts on the image of a man.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Virtues of birds and precious stones; bird familiars.

rows.name: Seere (Sear)
rows.office: Goes and comes; brings abundance of things to pass on a sudden; carries or re-carries anything to or from wherever wished; passes over the whole earth in the twinkling of an eye; gives a true relation of all sorts of theft, of treasure hid, and of many other things. Of an indifferent good nature and willing to do anything the exorcist desires.
rows.rank_text: a Mighty Prince, and Powerful, under AMAYMON, King of the East
rows.appearance: In the form of a beautiful man riding upon a winged horse.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Goes and returns in an instant; brings abundance; theft and hidden things. Good-natured; under Amaymon.

rows.name: Dantalion
rows.office: Teaches all arts and sciences to anyone; declares the secret counsels of anyone, for he knows the thoughts of all men and women and can change them at his will; causes love; shows the likeness of any person in a vision, wherever in the world they are.
rows.appearance: In the form of a man with many countenances, all men's and women's faces, with a book in his right hand.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: All arts and sciences; secret counsels; changes thoughts; causes love; shows likenesses of any person.

rows.name: Andromalius
rows.office: Brings back both the thief and the stolen goods; discovers all wickedness and underhand dealing; punishes all thieves and other wicked people; discovers hidden treasures.
rows.appearance: In the form of a man holding a great serpent in his hand.
rows.source: Mathers/Crowley, The Book of the Goetia of Solomon the King (1904)
rows.workbook_office: Returns thieves and stolen goods; discovers wickedness and underhand dealing; punishes thieves; hidden treasure.
